title: De Viris Illustribus Liber
author: Isidorus Hispalensis
source: Translated by Claude from tmp1425.tmp1425.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina.
statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.
availability: CC BY-SA 4.0, as its source requires: credit Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina and this AI translation, and share adaptations under the same licence.

passages.original: Hic longe ante beatissimum Augustinum edidit librum de Hæresibus, singulas quasque demonstrans, sive quae in popule Judaeorum ante incarnationem Christi furunt, quas viginti octo enumerat, sive quae post Domini adventum Salvaloris, adversus catholicam fidem exortae sunt, quas idem centum viginti octo esse describit, sicut de eo idem vir magnae gloriae Augustinus, et docto, clarissimus, meminit.
passages.english: Long before the most blessed Augustine, he published a book On Heresies, setting out each and every one of them, both those which raged among the people of the Jews before the incarnation of Christ, which he numbers at twenty-eight, and those which arose against the catholic faith after the coming of the Lord [our] Saviour, which he likewise describes as being one hundred and twenty-eight, just as that same man of great glory, Augustine, most learned and most illustrious, recalls concerning him.
passages.notes: Scanning errors read as intended: 'popule' as 'populo', 'furunt' as 'fuerunt' (or 'furuerunt', 'raged'), 'Salvaloris' as 'Salvatoris'. 'et docto, clarissimus' appears corrupt, perhaps for 'doctor clarissimus' ('most illustrious teacher'); rendered as 'most learned and most illustrious'.

passages.original: Marcellinus, Italiæ presbyter, scripsit Theodosio Minori, Arcadioque imperatoribus, opusculum unum, in quo retexit gesta episcoporum qui ad destructionem homousion Arimini convenerunt; quique ita totum mundum perfidia impii dogmatis turbaverunt, ut vix pauci antistites existerent qui in inviolabili fidei cultu perseverarent. Exponit quoque de Ario, dum ad synodum pergeret cum Alexandro disputaturus, qualiter conversus in via ad necessariam cau. sam, viscera ejus fuissent diffusa. De fine quoque Osii Cordubensis urbis episcopi, qui, metu imperatoris, fidem prevaricatus, perfidiae assertor et impietatis effectus fuerat 147 assecutor, sic talia profert.
passages.english: Marcellinus, a presbyter of Italy, wrote for the emperors Theodosius the Younger and Arcadius a single short work, in which he recounts the doings of the bishops who assembled at Ariminum for the destruction of the *homoousion* [the doctrine that the Son is of one substance with the Father], and who so disturbed the whole world with the faithlessness of their impious doctrine that there were scarcely a few bishops who persevered in the inviolable practice of the faith. He also relates of Arius how, while he was on his way to the synod to dispute with Alexander, he turned aside on the road to relieve himself, and his bowels poured out. Concerning the end of Hosius, bishop of the city of Córdoba, who out of fear of the emperor had betrayed the faith and had become an advocate of faithlessness and a follower of impiety, he also sets out the following.
passages.notes: 'cau. sam' is a scanning split for 'causam'; 'necessariam causam' is a euphemism for relieving nature. '147' is a page number from the printed edition and has been omitted. 'homousion' is given as a technical term. This notice is usually understood to refer to the work of Faustinus and Marcellinus (the 'Libellus precum'); the attribution and the order 'Theodosius Minor and Arcadius' are as the text has them, although that pairing is chronologically odd.

passages.original: 33. Hic tamen, in secundo ejusdem operis libro, Tertulliani erroribus consentiens, animam corpoream esse dixit, quibusdam hoc fallacibus argumentis astruere contendens. Edidit etiam unum libellum de Virginibus instituendis, alios quoque tres de futurae vitæ contemplatione, vel actuali conversatione, necnon de vitiis atque virtutibus.
passages.english: 33. This man, however, in the second book of the same work, agreeing with the errors of Tertullian, said that the soul is corporeal, striving to establish this with certain deceptive arguments. He also published one little book On the Instruction of Virgins, and three others as well, on the contemplation of the future life, or the active way of life, and also on vices and virtues.
passages.notes: The passage has no context, so the subject of 'Hic' is unidentified. 'vel actuali conversatione' may refer to a separate topic, the active life, rather than an alternative title.

passages.original: 39. Hilarius, Arelatensis episcopus, scripsit Vitam parentis et prædecessoris sui, sanctissimi ac venerabilis Honorati episcopi, suavi ac praeclaro prædicta- tam eloquio.
passages.english: 39. Hilary, bishop of Arles, wrote the Life of his father and predecessor, the most holy and venerable bishop Honoratus, set forth in sweet and splendid eloquence.
passages.notes: 'parentis' probably means spiritual father or kinsman rather than literal father. 'prædicta- tam' is read as 'prædicatam' ('proclaimed' or 'set forth').
